title: A Rice theorem for stationary states under fixed noise
description: Which macroscopic questions about a noisy lattice can an algorithm decide from its local rule? Fix dimension seven and one positive rational replacement rate. Every nontrivial property determined by the number of extreme translation-invariant stationary laws, all-law ergodicity, and the existence of a translation-invariant stationary law with nondecaying local covariance is undecidable. A stronger theorem retains the numbers of extreme translation-invariant stationary states with nondecaying covariance and with a Bragg atom at some nonzero wavevector. The same statements hold for finite-depth circuits of local quantum channels with fresh product ancillas, followed by whole-site depolarization. Under a stated published-source condition C_T, at another fixed rational rate the total-count cuts "at most r" and "at least k" are respectively Π⁰₂-complete for every r ≥ 1 and Σ⁰₂-complete for every k ≥ 2, in both categories. The scope has a decidable boundary: a classical translation-invariant stationary law attains the noise entropy floor exactly when the deterministic rule is constant.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. The authors have not independently verified the mathematical arguments; the paper's section 'How this work was done' describes the model-based construction and the cross-family checks.
